A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Esoteric Language Models. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison; visual inspection resolved extraction ambiguities. Renamed models and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original LM1B and OWT experiments, generation-quality and timing measurements, zero-shot evaluations, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds importance-weighted likelihood evaluations, sampler experiments, MAUVE measurements, and long-context generation results.

M1.justification: The core hybrid objective, attention mechanisms, and KV caching are retained: v1's Eso-LM (B) becomes Eso-LMs, while variant (A) moves to Appendix D. V2 adds single-pass any-order likelihood computation with importance-weighted aggregation (Section 3.3, Appendix B.8) and a heuristic sampler that decodes widely spaced positions together (Appendix E.6), substantially extending scoring and inference.

E1.justification: Both versions use LM1B and OWT and retain the same zero-shot coverage: PTB, Wikitext, LM1B, Lambada, AG News, Pubmed, and Arxiv. The added 10,240-token experiment extends sequence length and fine-tuning within existing OWT language-generation coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds an AR baseline with AdaLN on both primary benchmarks and adds BD3-LMs with block sizes 4 and 8 to the OWT likelihood comparison, where v1 reported only block size 16. The principal comparator families and zero-shot comparator membership remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The main generation evaluation changes from single-sample timing on A6000 to batches of 512 on H200, adds MAUVE using ModernBERT-Large, and specifies 5,120 generated samples. MDLM and BD3 generation comparisons change from 1M-step to 250K-step models. V2 also introduces importance-weighted likelihood evaluation, broader sampling configurations, and 1,000-step fine-tuning at context length 10,240.

E4.justification: V2 adds sensitivity studies over the number of sampled likelihood orderings, comparisons of the heuristic sampler against ordinary sampling, and dedicated diffusion-only-model Pareto analyses. It extends the attention ablation on OWT and supplies generated-text examples illustrating quality differences. The original batch-split and BD3 sample-selection analyses remain present.

E5.justification: Speed-quality timing changes from the median across five trials in v1 Section 5.3 to the mean across ten trials in v2 Section 5.2. Long-context timing retains five-run mean and standard-deviation reporting, including the added experiment. Neither version reports confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Reported NELBO perplexities change, including LM1B Eso-LM (B) at alpha0=1 from 35.00 to 36.12 and OWT MDLM from 25.76 to 25.19. Several zero-shot baseline rows change while Eso-LM rows remain identical. V2 adds importance-weighted, MAUVE, sampler, and 10,240-token results and removes the earlier 1M-step OWT likelihood column. Generation scores are replaced under revised evaluation settings, so their differences do not establish same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Beyond the retained hybrid NELBO, v2 introduces importance-weighted bounds over denoising permutations, proves monotonic tightening and convergence to negative log likelihood, and extends the argument to hybrid models (Theorem 3.1 and Appendix B.2–B.3). These are substantive mathematical additions absent from v1.

C1.justification: V2 promotes single-pass NELBO evaluation and the claimed first exact MDM likelihood computation to central contributions. Its abstract and introduction replace the earlier emphasis on state-of-the-art diffusion perplexity with likelihood-computation capabilities and explicit speed-quality positioning. Hybrid interpolation, parallel KV caching, and the long-context speedup claims are retained.

C2.justification: V2 recommends diffusion-only training with inference-time schedule adjustment, replacing v1's recommendation of different training mixtures for different budgets. It adds the qualification that perplexity reflects infinite-budget generation, discusses suitability for reinforcement learning, and explicitly compares training overhead. The earlier teacher-forcing explanation for BD3 degradation is dropped, while the existing neighboring-token-conflict explanation receives greater emphasis.

D1.justification: V2 adds FlexAttention mask code, a transformer implementation listing, likelihood-evaluation compute details, checkpoint provenance, and announced video tutorials. OWT training times are revised from approximately 50/69 hours to 27/37 hours. These substantially expand documentation, although Figure 13 concatenates clean and noisy inputs in the opposite order to Section 4.1.2, leaving an implementation inconsistency.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around any-order autoregression, importance-weighted estimation, and reinforcement learning. Section 6 adds comparisons with concurrent caching methods by Hu, Wu, and Ma, distinguishes Xue's architecture, and relates Pannatier and Xue to its full-diffusion case. These substantive relationships go beyond the accompanying citation-style changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, background, method exposition, experimental narrative, and discussion undergo extensive rewriting. Section 4 is reorganized around training and sampling instead of two model variants, variant (A) moves to a dedicated appendix, and speed-quality evaluation precedes long-context latency. Boxed findings and remarks further restructure the narrative.

P2.justification: V2 adds a front-page feature summary, a training illustration and cost chart, likelihood-evaluation diagrams, code figures, MAUVE plots, and generated-text panels. Attention diagrams are redrawn and separated by variant. The primary likelihood tables are merged with separate Exact and NELBO columns, while the original long-context timing table is relocated intact.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the speed-quality evidence through matched 250K-step generation comparisons, complementary MAUVE measurements, and long-context quality evaluation, while clarifying implementation and limitations. However, its newly promoted exact-likelihood results use finite K, whereas the theorem guarantees equality only as K tends to infinity and Tables 5–6 still vary with K. Figure 13 also contradicts the stated input order. These new reporting and reproducibility problems limit the net quality gain despite the substantial revision.
